core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Hamed corresponds to the Arabic form حامد (Arabic root ح م د (ḥ-m-d); حَامِد (Ḥāmid)). Its core sense is praiseworthy, commendable, laudable. Hamed is a transliteration of Arabic حَامِد (Ḥāmid) 'one who praises, praiser', the active participle of the root ح م د (ḥ-m-d). The source gloss 'praised, commended' describes the passive participle مَحْمُود/حَمِيد rather than this form; 'one who praises' is the sense of حامد. The word حامد appears in the Qur'an.
